Primary: CNBC quote endpoint, read 07:53 BST. Cross-check: Trading Economics (UK 10Y, US 10Y, Brent).

*** PRE-OPEN: THREE INSTRUMENTS CARRY TUESDAY'S CLOSES ***
Read before the London open, so FTSE, S&P 500 and VIX carry Tuesday's closes with Tuesday's session
moves, declared. The FTSE feed lag inside the first half-hour is now established beyond argument and
Trading Economics is not a usable second provider pre-open.
  FTSE 10,650.33 -0.06 | SP 7,805.45 -0.02 | VIX 15.27 +0.39
Two of those differ from what last night's edition published, because last night's were live intraday
values read at 19:25 while Wall Street was still open, and these are the settled closes:
  SP   published 7,804.03 intraday -> actual close 7,805.45
  VIX  published 15.44 intraday    -> actual close 15.27
Neither is an error in last night's edition; an intraday read and a close are different things, and the
close is the right figure this morning. The VIX change of +0.39 is computed against Monday's 15.21 so
that all three lagged instruments share one basis.

*** GILT: DOWN AGAIN, AND THIS TIME THE PROVIDERS AGREE ***
  CNBC:              5.4047, change -0.049 (on prev 5.4537)  -> -0.05
  Trading Economics: 5.40,   day change -0.036                -> -0.04
  Our own series:    5.40 against last night's published 5.44 -> -0.04
PUBLISHED: 5.40, -0.04. Trading Economics and our own series agree; CNBC's figure rests on a prev of
5.4537, which is the same value its prev field has been serving for three days and which we established
on Monday is about 2bp above the real close. Two bases against one, and the two that agree are the ones
that have been reliable.
Worth recording what this instrument has done in forty-eight hours: 5.44 Monday close, 5.38 Tuesday
morning, back to 5.44 by Tuesday's close, now 5.40. That is a 6bp round trip followed by a 4bp fall, in
a yield sitting near its highest since 2007 fifteen days before a Budget. Yesterday morning's drivers
called a fall "the sharpest in weeks" and the day erased it; this morning's drivers say only where it is.

*** UST ***
  CNBC: 5.19, -0.027 (prev 5.217) | Trading Economics: 5.20, -0.022 | Our series: 5.22 -> 5.19 = -0.03
PUBLISHED: 5.19, -0.03 — the CNBC live level, with the change consistent against our own published
series. TE rounds the level to 5.20 and the change to -0.02; the difference is sub-basis-point rounding
and is recorded rather than hidden.

*** BRENT: FLAT TO FIRMER DESPITE AN ARAMCO BUILDING BEING HIT ***
105.89, up 0.19% on a Tuesday settle of 105.69. Overnight an Aramco building was struck in Dhahran and
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh and Dhahran — and crude has barely moved. That
is the fourth consecutive session in which Gulf escalation has produced less in the oil price than the
headlines would imply, and it is worth saying so rather than implying a premium that is not there.
CROSS-CHECK: Trading Economics 105.92 +0.22% against CNBC 105.89 +0.19%. Agreement. WTI 94.25 +0.12%.
